title: Customer Churn Prediction
description: An end-to-end machine learning application that analyzes customer behavior and predicts customer churn using data preprocessing, exploratory analysis, and predictive modeling to help identify customers at risk of leaving.
dataset: Telco Customer Churn Dataset (7,043 customers, 21 attributes)
businessProblem: Identify telecom customers at risk of leaving (churning) based on demographics, tenure, subscription services, and billing contracts, enabling targeted retention interventions.
workflow: Data ingestion and type coercion (converting blank TotalCharges to numerical 0 for new customers)
Exploratory data analysis uncovering tenure, monthly charges, and contract duration associations
Stratified 80/20 train-test split preserving the 26.54% churn base rate
ColumnTransformer pipeline with median imputation & StandardScaler for numericals, and most-frequent imputation & OneHotEncoder for categoricals
Benchmarking baseline DummyClassifier against Logistic Regression, KNN, Decision Tree, and SVM
Hyperparameter optimization with GridSearchCV on Logistic Regression (C=0.1, class_weight='balanced') and SVM
Test set evaluation on 1,409 holdout customers achieving 78.61% recall and 0.8408 ROC-AUC
Serialization to joblib pipeline and interactive deployment via Streamlit
results: Achieved 74.17% test accuracy, 78.61% churn recall, and 0.8408 ROC-AUC on 1,409 holdout customer records, prioritizing recall to detect customers at risk of cancellation.
lessonsLearned: In customer retention, false negatives (failing to detect a churner) are costlier than false positives. Applying class_weight='balanced' boosted churn recall from 54.38% to 78.61%.
